Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b04/review-experiment-yv2d17im/call-07c32200844f4025b4078261bcb36aff/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la . && ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, shutil
for m in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
 s=importlib.util.find_spec(m)
 print(m,s.origin if s else None)
for p in ['pdftotext','pdftoppm','pdfinfo','gs']:
 print(p,shutil.which(p))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGE COUNT',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
text=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 s=p.extract_text()
 text.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n\\n{s}')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(s)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(text))
print(''.join(text[:3]))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re, statistics
s=Path('tmp/pdfs/page-07.txt').read_text().split('LLaMA2/ChatGPT on MRPC dataset)')[0]
x=[int(i) for i in re.findall(r'\\+\\s*(\\d+)%',s)]
print('Finite percentage increases extracted from Table 2:',len(x))
print('Mean:',statistics.mean(x),'Median:',statistics.median(x),'Range:',(min(x),max(x)))
for p in ['page-03.txt','page-04.txt','page-06.txt','page-10.txt']:
 print('\\n'+p)
 print(Path('tmp/pdfs/'+p).read_text())
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses a useful, clearly motivated NLP question: how much labelled data smaller specialised models need to compete with prompted larger models. Studying learning curves between extreme few-shot and full-data settings has practical value.

The comparison covers seven models, eight datasets, and four approaches. Repeated experiments—100 runs for fine-tuning, generally 20 for other approaches, and 10 for ChatGPT—provide substantially better evidence about variability than single-run comparisons.

Figure 2 and Table 2 provide useful evidence that smaller models can become competitive with modest training sets on several classification tasks. Reporting dataset-specific crossovers, cases without crossovers, and both absolute and relative increases helps expose important variation behind aggregate results.
The manuscript provides a source-code link, prompt templates, principal training hyperparameters, and candid disclosures about computational constraints and evaluation limitations.
weaknesses: The annotation-budget interpretation is unresolved. Section 3 reserves 20% of all available labelled examples for validation and uses early stopping, but does not explain whether validation labels are counted or restricted as the training budget decreases. Consequently, results with 10 or 100 training examples do not establish that the same total number of annotations suffices. This matters directly for the practical recommendations; validation supervision must be accounted for, with an appropriate budget-controlled comparison.

The documented prompts raise a concrete validity concern. Table 1 describes BoolQ as determining whether a passage contains an answer, whereas BoolQ requires answering the question itself with yes or no. These are different targets. More generally, one prompt engineered on Mistral, combined with an unspecified output-to-label mapping, is insufficiently checked given that prompt performance determines every crossover. The executed prompts should be clarified, task mismatches corrected, and affected comparisons rerun with a limited robustness check.

The central variance-adjusted crossover is insufficiently defined. Section 3.2 does not specify an exact mathematical criterion or how precise thresholds are obtained between exponentially spaced training sizes. Figure 1 suggests comparing standard-deviation bands, but their non-overlap does not itself establish a calibrated probability of outperformance or a worst-case guarantee. The paper should distinguish run-to-run variability from uncertainty in estimated means and define either a probabilistic criterion or an explicitly heuristic interpretation before treating the reported percentage increases as reliable quantitative guidance.

Prior supervised benchmark exposure is not addressed. FLAN-T5's instruction-tuning history makes an overlap audit particularly important when all available benchmark examples are redistributed into new training, validation, and test sets. Previously seen examples could enter evaluation. This needs investigation before interpreting strong performance with 10 additional examples as evidence of adaptation to a new task with that label budget.

Several conclusions exceed the evidence. Section 3.1 states that at most 100 examples suffice to outperform every comparator on multiclass datasets, but Table 2 reports mean crossovers of 350 and 550 examples against FLAN-T5 on AG News, increasing to 1,100 with variance considered. Moreover, class count is confounded with task semantics and difficulty across the selected datasets. Recommendations about optimal computational trade-offs also lack comparative cost measurements. These claims should be narrowed to the observed configurations.

Important reproducibility details remain unspecified, including LoRA configuration, input truncation, generation parsing, and handling of two demonstrations per class when the available pool is too small. The restricted large-model evaluation disclosed later—1,000 test examples and a single 1,000-example training-pool setting—also needs integration into the main protocol, including clarification of whether methods share evaluation examples. Together with the label-budget, prompt-validity, and crossover-definition concerns, these gaps require correction and targeted validation before a sound Findings recommendation.
